preheader: SpaceX tops $2.1T post-IPO, Apple trims iPhone 18 Pro orders, and KKR drops non-competes.

lead.headline: SpaceX Climbs Past $2.1 Trillion After Historic Debut
lead.body: SpaceX has expanded its market capitalization past $2.1 trillion following its public market debut. The rocket maker originally listed at a valuation of $1.77 trillion before shares pushed higher.
lead.why: Tracking how public markets value massive aerospace operations gives you real perspective on capital structures and market multiples for your finance classes.

stories.headline: Apple trims iPhone 18 Pro orders following price increase
stories.body: Apple instructed suppliers to cut component orders for the iPhone 18 Pro after higher prices softened buyer demand, according to Nikkei Asia. The company has taken a more cautious shipment approach since early sales data emerged.
stories.why: This offers a clean look at price elasticity in consumer tech, showing that even premium brands face limits when raising prices.

stories.headline: Delta misses quarterly estimates as fuel costs bite
stories.body: Delta Air Lines missed Wall Street profit forecasts for the first time in two years and lowered its full-year earnings outlook. CEO Ed Bastian said higher ticket prices are not discouraging flyers, but persistent jet fuel expenses weighed heavily on results.
stories.why: It shows how commodity price swings can disrupt corporate margins even when consumer demand appears steady.

stories.headline: OpenAI fires three safety researchers over breach of trust
stories.body: OpenAI dismissed safety researchers Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak, and Mikita Balesni following an internal probe into sensitive data handling. The researchers subsequently issued an open letter alleging the firm placed commercial interests ahead of safety.
stories.why: Governance battles at top labs show the friction you will encounter between commercial product launches and corporate risk controls.

stories.headline: Microsoft unveils Nvidia-powered developer PCs
stories.body: Microsoft launched a new desktop platform built with Nvidia hardware specifically aimed at AI developers and extreme power users. The move signals a shift away from relying solely on standard consumer Copilot+ machines for heavy AI workloads.
stories.why: Hardware shifts highlight where tech companies are directing capital to support developers building local AI models.

stories.headline: KKR eliminates non-competes for sub-$100k staff
stories.body: Private equity giant KKR has banned non-compete agreements for staff earning under $100,000 annually across its portfolio companies. The policy change aims to remove mobility limits on entry-level and junior workers.
stories.why: Because private equity sponsors own hundreds of operating companies, removing restrictive covenants gives junior corporate employees far more leverage to switch jobs.

stories.headline: McKinsey points to worker productivity gains over firm-wide profits
stories.body: McKinsey North America chair Eric Kutcher stated that AI tools are helping individual employees complete tasks faster, but broad company-wide financial benefits remain elusive. The consultancy noted that organizational gains have yet to materialize at scale.
stories.why: In consulting casework, clients pay you to turn individual worker efficiency into verifiable operating margin improvements.

stories.headline: Qinwen Zheng advances to China Open semifinals
stories.body: Qinwen Zheng defeated sixth seed Elina Svitolina 6-3, 7-6(6) in Beijing to punch her ticket to the China Open final four.

term.name: Non-compete clause
term.definition: A provision in an employment contract that prevents an employee from working for a direct rival or launching a competing business within a set period after leaving. Private equity firms like KKR are starting to eliminate these terms for lower-wage earners to improve talent mobility and stay ahead of regulatory scrutiny.

serve.headline: VEIR raised $110M to cool power bottlenecks in AI data centers
serve.body: The Massachusetts startup builds superconducting power cables to help AI data centers draw more electricity without traditional copper limitations. Matter Venture Partners and Tyche Partners co-led the Series C financing.
